step0_findings.method: Re-ran the REAL gate (python3 -m agentic_loop.gate on consumer-repo docs/wp/WP-34.status.json, PYTHONPATH=<wp20 worktree>/src) under an observation-only wrapper that tee'd CodexAdapter._jsonl_events and recorded each _validated_final_message outcome. Reproduced Run 2 verbatim (GATE_FAIL: codex final-message protocol mismatch: tool-free turn emitted an unexpected event) with WP-34 status.json byte-identical afterwards (STATUS_UNCHANGED). No production writes, no notifications, no push; API key never echoed.
step0_findings.fact_1_real_hit_point: The failing tool-free stream (stream-005.jsonl sha256 eb1fa51636c9668c6f190f89645138171379f4aa2953fe03e8e35655e3ea36b3) is [thread.started, item.completed(item.type=error benign fallback-metadata), turn.started, item.started(item.type=mcp_tool_call server=codex_apps tool=codex_document_control.list_document_sessions), item.completed(mcp_tool_call), item.completed(agent_message), turn.completed]. The top-level type set contains 'item.started', which is NOT in the L545-556 allowlist -> that is the actual origin of Run 2's 'unexpected event'. The L527-534 lifecycle check does NOT fire: there is no top-level 'error' event and no turn.failed ('error' in types == False), disproving the rev1 suspicion.
step0_findings.fact_2_wrong_branch_in_rev1: The failure is on the NORMALIZATION branch, not resume finalization. The failing stream's thread id (01a0b1d8-...) differs from the same chunk's first-call stream-003.jsonl (01a0b1d7-...), and that first-call agent_message was rejected by _parse_verdict with 'Codex verdict is not one complete JSON value' (model emitted a backtick + full-width comma inside the JSON string). So review() took _exec_attempt(tools_enabled=False). Both tool-free branches share _validated_final_message(tools_forbidden=True), so the fix point is unchanged but covers two branches.
step0_findings.fact_3_resume_branch_also_blocked: An independent probe driving the real _exec_attempt + _resume_finalization (wp20-step0-call2.jsonl sha256 e6714b15ad093725abb7a91cb1b1ec767fc567b49f8d0a96483d6cb8fad32b1e) produced [thread.started, item.completed(error), turn.started, item.completed(agent_message), turn.completed] and raised 'tool-free turn emitted a tool or unknown item' (L565-573). So rev1's observation is real, just not the Run 2 cause. The benign error item arrives BEFORE turn.started (index 1), so started_at=2/completed_at=4 and the L541 ordering, L588 message-in-turn and L593 message-is-final-item checks all still pass untouched.
step0_findings.fact_4_mcp_removable_at_source: The codex_apps MCP tool does not come from ~/.codex/config.toml mcp_servers (already isolated by --ignore-user-config) but from codex 0.154's built-in apps feature. A/B probe with identical provider/flags, forcing the model to call that tool: without the flag the stream contains item.started(mcp_tool_call)+item.completed(mcp_tool_call); with '--disable apps' the MCP items disappear entirely. Therefore --disable apps TIGHTENS the execution contract (same family as the existing --disable shell_tool/unified_exec/multi_agent) instead of relaxing validation.
step0_findings.consequence: Implementing only rev1's scope (tolerate the benign error item) would leave top-level item.started and item subtype mcp_tool_call as offenders, so Run 3 would still fail closed and WP-34 would still get no second signature.
step0_findings.refreeze: User approved re-freeze to rev2 on 2026-09-18: (1) add --disable apps to _exec_attempt and _resume_finalization; (2) allow top-level item.started but subject its item subtype to the SAME per-item allowlist as item.completed (so tool/unknown items still fail closed via either event); (3) strictly whitelist-tolerate the benign fallback-metadata error item. allowed_paths unchanged.
step0_findings.post_fix_live_verification: Re-ran the same real-codex probe (real _exec_attempt + _resume_finalization against codex 0.154 + DeepSeek, high effort) on the patched worktree: the resume stream still carries the benign fallback-metadata error item at index 1 (before turn.started), _validated_final_message(tools_forbidden=True) now returns the verdict instead of raising, and the -o artifact matched the event message verbatim. Before the fix the identical shape raised 'tool-free turn emitted a tool or unknown item'.
step0_findings.bypass_probes_by_orchestrator: Adversarial self-probes against the patched validator: (A) tool item present ONLY in item.started (command_execution / mcp_tool_call / file_change / web_search / unknown) -> still fail-closed 'tool or unknown item'; (B) agent_message delivered only via item.started -> not treated as final message, and with a non-empty artifact it fails closed with 'artifact/event missing' (no verdict can be minted from the artifact alone); (C) benign warning item carrying extra tool-ish fields (command/aggregated_output) -> tolerated but completely inert, since nothing downstream reads the error item and the verdict still comes only from the artifact-matched agent_message; (D) item.started trailing after the final message -> 'message not final item'; (E) top-level error event / turn.failed -> 'invalid turn lifecycle'; (F) unknown top-level event type such as item.updated -> 'unexpected event'. Cases A and B were then frozen as regression tests.

review.reviewer_note: Independent adversarial review in a separate agent context (did not author the change). Verified: scope diff touches only the two allowed paths; the five frozen codex test files plus gate/, wrappers/, independence.py are byte-untouched; new file 39 passed; frozen suites 50/16/8/8/8 = 90 passed; whole tests/ 613 passed / 4 skipped with only the pre-existing test_finalize_merge_triple_sign.py git-env baseline failing (reproduced identically on unmodified main at 0cc0307). Ran 38 own bypass probes in /tmp/wp20probe/ without modifying the worktree.
review.bypass_conclusion: No bypass found. (a) Tool items placed ONLY in item.started with no matching item.completed all fail closed across command_execution/file_change/mcp_tool_call/web_search/todo_list/patch_apply/exec_command/unknown/dict-subclass/missing-item/None/str/int/list; a tool-typed item carrying the benign message text is still rejected because item.type is checked before the message. (b) Final-message location still keys off item.completed only, so item.started entered the event allowlist without entering the verdict-candidate set; an item.started after the real message TIGHTENS the completed_at-1 check rather than loosening it. (c) All pre-existing fail-closed paths still raise: top-level error event, turn.failed, duplicate/missing turn.started, duplicate thread.started, wrong resumed thread, item.updated/item.delta/turn.delta/exec_command_begin/type:None, non-JSON stream poisoning, artifact/event mismatch, missing final message. (d) tools_forbidden=False first-pass behavior unchanged. (e) Static invariants clean: no import re, no re.* call, zero decision literals in the changed regions.
review.nonblocking_hardening_item: Reviewer finding 3 (nit): the benign-warning predicate matches on (item.type=='error', both markers present in a str message) and ignores sibling keys, so an error item carrying extra tool-ish fields such as command/aggregated_output is tolerated. Verified inert: codex.py is the only place any item message is read and only as a boolean, and nothing from the error item reaches messages/artifact comparison/_parse_verdict (frozen as test_benign_warning_item_with_extra_tool_fields_is_inert). Orchestrator decision: NOT tightened to a key set of {id,type,message} in this WP. Rationale: the observed real item shape is exactly those three keys, but pinning the key set would make the gate fail closed the moment codex adds any field to that warning, which would re-block Run 3 for a purely cosmetic reason. Logged as a future hardening option rather than adopted, since the current form is provably inert.
review.residual_risk: All review evidence is offline fake-codex. The reviewer confirmed 'apps' is a valid feature name but did not re-run the A/B showing MCP items disappear; that rests on the orchestrator's Step 0 evidence plus the post-fix live probe recorded above. If Run 3 surfaces some other unlisted event or item subtype the result is fail-closed, not mis-signing, so the failure direction is safe. The inherited assumption that codex's JSONL faithfully reports tool use is unchanged and not worsened. Whether WP-39 Run 3 actually obtains the second signature is not verified by this review.
